A handwritten card in small, neat lettering. Use to invite Li Wu tomorrow.
Ivory cardstock with a faint sandalwood scent. Use to invite Wen Qi tomorrow.
A scuffed metal card edged with blue tape. Use to invite Pei Jia tomorrow.

I brought you something.
...This is for you.
Let's see what you brought.
Let's discuss today's rarities and sought-after pieces.
It's yours.
...Let me think about it.
Go ahead. Have a look.
I don't buy that.
Deal.
Until next time.
...All right. You're right. Your price it is.|Sharp eyes. Fine, I'll give a little.
What are you talking about? There's nothing wrong with it.|Look more carefully before making accusations.
No room on the counter. I'll bring the rest another time.
This watch checks out.
Something's wrong with this watch. My offer reflects what it really is.
Oh? Put it on the scale. Let me see.
Is this... for me?
Then never mind.
I don't want this. Take it back.
...How did you know I wanted this? Thank you. Truly.
Nice. I'll take it.
Thanks.
...You're giving this as a gift? Fine.
If you're short on credits, we can talk another time.
All right.
Hey, boss! I'm Ruan Deng. I flip secondhand watches.//Entry-level only, and pretty comes first. Real or fake? That's on whoever's looking.
Hey, boss! How's your luck today?|Back again! Yours is my favorite shop on this street.
Hey! I was thinking about your counter the whole way here.|Li Wu says your bench work is getting good, so I hurried over~
Miss me, boss? I made a special detour.|I tell my customers yours are the most reliable watches on this street. Don't make me look bad!
Take your pick. We can work out a price!|I picked every one of these for the colors. Look around~
Not this one. My customers want entry-level watches that look fresh.|Too expensive for me to resell. Keep it.|Parts missing? How am I supposed to sell that?
Deal! I like someone who gets to the point.|Yay!|Deal~ I'll be back.
I'm off! I'll come treasure hunting again soon.|Bye~ Save me the pretty ones!
Oh... you noticed. Fine, a little cheaper.|Your eyes are too sharp! All right, your price.
Huh? I checked it when I bought it... Don't make things up.|No way! I showed it to Li Wu... I think?
For me? Yes, yes, put it on the scale!
Wow, is that really for me?
Oh, not giving it after all? Okay~
Oh my goodness! This is gorgeous!//That's it. From now on, you get first pick of my best stock.|How did you know I wanted this!//When my customers ask, I'm telling them it was from you~
Thanks, boss! I'll wear it well.|So cute! I'm keeping it~
Well... thanks.|Oh, okay. I can always flip it.
Uh, a gun? What would I do with this... I'll keep it, I guess.
I really can't use this. You keep it.
By the way, don't force a broken watch open.//I know a watchmaker, Li Wu. She's very good.//I'll ask her to stop by in a couple of days!
Li Wu. Watchmaker. Ruan Deng mentioned your shop.//If you don't have a proper bench yet, I brought one. Use it.//Take your time with the tools. No prying. Fit an adapter ring before you mix models.
Li Wu. I was passing by.|We meet again.
Good to see you. Any recent purchases you're unsure about?|Did Ruan Deng buy another quartz as mechanical? ...Thought so.
Sit down. ...Kidding. It's your shop.|Your work is improving.|Wen Qi asked me to pass it on: she was pleased with that last piece.
The parts have markings. Compare them yourself.|Read the markings first. Then we talk.
At least the movement and dial must be genuine. Case and strap, I don't mind.|Replica part. I won't buy it.
Deal.|Fine.|Good. Handle it gently.
I'm off. Keep your watches away from magnets.|Leaving. Wipe the prints off the bridges.
...You're right. Missed it when I bought it. Your price.
No. Look at the markings and bridges again. This part is fine.
Had a look. Genuine parts. No issue.
Wait. Let me open it... Yes, the internals are wrong. Price it accordingly.
For me? Put it on the scale.
...For me?
This movement... very well maintained.//Thank you. Your watches get priority from now on.
Genuine work. Thank you. I'll take it.|Good piece. I'll keep it. It'll come in handy.
I'll keep it for spares.
This doesn't meet my requirements. ...I appreciate the thought.|...Next time, bring a genuine non-quartz part.
Only watches and parts, thanks.
Could you inspect these watches? ({0} watches, {1} credits)
Done. {1} of the {0} watches have problems. I've marked them. Have a look.
If you find a good, fully genuine watch, don't sell it to Ruan Deng. She can't afford it.//Let me introduce Wen Qi. She only buys genuine pieces, but she pays generously.
A modder named Pei Jia is looking for help.//Strange requests, prompt payment. I'll send her your way.
Li Wu left you a precision watch workbench.

A pleasure. I'm Wen Qi. Li Wu says genuine pieces occasionally turn up here.//I'm fond of higher-end watches: all four parts genuine, from one model, in good condition.//Don't worry. I'll treat you fairly.
Good afternoon. Forgive the intrusion again.|Good afternoon. Yours is still the quietest shop on this street.
We meet again. Have you checked this week's market?|I've been thinking about that last watch of yours.|I've read this week's auction catalog three times. Your counter is still more interesting.
Coming here is the part of my week I look forward to most.|Li Wu says your buying has become very precise. I'm glad for you.
Take your time. Inspect it before we discuss the price.|No rush. Look at every piece carefully first.
Sorry. Only genuine, matching-model pieces in good condition.|This one... isn't for my collection.
A fine transaction. Thank you.|A pleasure, as always.
I should go. Until next time.|A lovely afternoon. I'll bring some tea next time.
...An oversight on my part. Your price, then. My apologies.
I inspected this one myself. Please look again.
All original... beautifully preserved.
A pity. One component isn't original. I'll need to reconsider the price.
A gift for me? I would be honored.
This... is for me?
That's all right. The thought is enough.
Original, matching serials... and in this condition.//I don't know how to thank you. If you ever need anything, just ask.
You chose thoughtfully. Thank you.|I'm glad you remembered what I like.
Thank you for thinking of me.
...There are replica parts in this. Were you deceived, too?
Thank you, but I don't collect these.
A friend would like to meet you: Shen Yuan, a private auction adviser.//She only handles the finest original pieces. More particular than I am.//But... she knows things others don't.
So you're the boss who takes watches apart? I'm Pei Jia.//Original? That's for display cases. A watch should look the way you want it to.//I'll bring work your way. It pays.
Here I am!|Hey, boss. Fingers itching today?
Loved your last modification.|Hey, partner. Itchy fingers lately?|Purists like Wen Qi? We live on different planets.
Old partner! Just landed a big order. Thought I'd stop by.|In a good mood today. Let's chat.|Li Wu says my builds are too loud. What does she know, heh.
Take your pick. I don't haggle... kidding. We can haggle.|See one you like? Say so. I don't haggle long with straight shooters.
No quartz. I want a mechanical watch that breathes.|Too low-end. Not worth modifying.
That's the spirit!|Deal, partner.|Done!
I'm off. Save the interesting jobs for me.|Gone! Think of me when your fingers itch.
Tch. Saw right through it. Fine, your price.
Come on. I've been doing this for over a decade. It's fine.
For me? Let's see it!
Oh? Let me look.
Tch. Way to tease me.
Damn, that custom work has character!//You're my personal watch modder now.
Interesting. I'll take it!|Nice. Just my kind of thing.
Not bad. Thanks.|A bit plain, but good bones.
Quartz? ...Not my thing.
I only play with watches. Keep the rest.
Any custom orders lately?

Got one. The client wants a {0} with the {1} changed to a {2}.//All four parts genuine and matching, condition eighty or better. The client has sharp eyes.//Deliver before day {3}. Reward: {4}, every credit.
Remind me of the order requirements?
{0}, with {1} {2}. All genuine, matching parts, condition at least eighty. Deadline: day {3}. Don't forget.
Your custom watch is ready.
...Perfect. Exactly the feel I wanted.//Here's {0}. Keep it safe.
Wen Qi sent you? I'm Shen Yuan.//I only touch top-tier originals with matching serials, in near-perfect condition.//Don't show me anything else.
I'm short on time.|Let's keep this brief.
Your eye is better than I expected.|There are rumors at the auction house... Never mind. Business first.
I feel like staying a while, for once. It's quieter here than at the auction house.|The auction house took in a few fakes lately, under respectable names. Not here, I trust.
It's on the counter. I don't haggle. Neither should you.
Not original with matching serials? No discussion.|Condition isn't good enough.
Acceptable.|Done. Don't mention my name outside.
Goodbye.|I'm leaving.
...I misjudged it. Your price.
Be certain before you speak.
Original, matching serials. Good.
Opened, or parts replaced. I won't pay that.
A gift? I rarely accept them. Put it here.
...Are you sure?
Just as well.
...Even the auction house rarely sees one of these.//I owe you a favor. I don't say that often.
I'll accept it.|Not bad. I'll have it appraised... a joke.
Hm.
I don't wear non-original pieces.
No need.

There's something you should know.//Someone travels this route. Ying Xiyuan. Nobody knows where she comes from.//She recognizes one watch: a Bellor movement and dial in a Rydor case and strap.//To meet her, burn Forbidden Court Essence. I have a bottle. It isn't cheap.

Boss, spare me some counter space. Gold Viper. I deal in... things best kept out of sight.//Weapons, drugs. Good quality, I'll buy. Labels mean nothing to me. I judge the goods.//I always carry Vita-Stabilizer Capsules. A certain little creature follows their scent.
Business looks good, boss.|We meet again. Anything worthwhile today?
That impatient Crimson Falcon was here? Her stock isn't as clean as mine.|Watch yourself, boss. Things are getting tense.|Crimson Falcon's been buying in a hurry. Another rush job, I'd bet.
Your shop feels safer than my safe house.|Brought you something nice. Don't say it came from me.|When people ask about your shop, I say I've never heard of it. That's a compliment.
Take a look. We can discuss the price.
I don't touch poor-condition goods or unclear provenance.|This quality... Boss, are you testing me?
A pleasure doing business.|Paid in full, boss.|This deal never happened.
I'm leaving. Don't see me out.|Don't see me out. Someone's watching the door.
Sharp eyes. Fine, your price.|Well, boss. I'll remember that eye of yours.
Accusations have a price, boss.
A gift? I like gifts.
Oh? For me?
Not giving it? Teasing is a bad habit, boss.
Star Coral... Know what this fetches on the black market?//I won't forget this favor.
Good taste.|This will buy a lot of favors out there.
I'll take it.|This piece? ...Fine. Someone will need it.
...Boss. This is your idea of a gift?
I'll pass.
Relax. Those case files will lose themselves.//Keep a low profile for a while.
Suppress case: halve crime/evidence, cancel queued enforcement ({0} credits)
Crimson Falcon. Here to buy.//Weapons. Drugs. Decent quality will do.//Brought capsules, too. If you don't need them, someone will.
Open for business. Good.|Goods are here. Make it quick.
That snake Gold Viper stopped by? Don't trust her prices.|Last batch was good. More of that today.|Don't trust the snake's prices. Don't fully trust mine either.
One of the few places I trust, this shop.|No rush today. ...Take your time.|...That last gun saved my life.
Look at the goods.
No.|Not this.
Fine.|Deal.|We're square.
Leaving.|Leaving. Lock up.
...Fine. Your price.
Watch your mouth.
A gift? Put it here.
For me?
...Suit yourself.
Sovereign Armor...//...Thanks. This time, I mean it.
Good hardware. I'll take it.|Well kept. I'll use it.
Hm.|As long as it works.
What's this?
No.
Done. The people watching you will be busy for a while.
...Medicine. I can smell it.//Vita-Stabilizer Capsules. Sell them to me.//I'm... Bai E. Designation T-03. Don't ask anything else.
...Medicine... give me medicine...|Hands... shaking. Please. Capsules.
Back again. Same medicine.|...Thank you for the capsules. I'm still alive.
Feeling better. Brought you something to say thanks.|I remember your shop. ...That doesn't happen often.
My strength is returning. I can feel it.//I brought these back. Have a look.|You never asked where I came from. ...Thank you.|Gold Viper calls me ‘little creature’. ...I hit harder than she does.
I'm fully recovered.//I used to be a number. Now I'd like to be a customer.|Good things today. And if you need help, ask me.|I used to know only numbers. Now I know this street, and your door.
Your choice.
Only capsules.
...Thank you.|Mm. Deal. ...I learned that word.
I'll go. Next time... I'll come back.|I'm going. Nobody followed you outside. I checked.
...You're right.
I don't understand this. Don't yell at me.
...For me?
This is for me?
...Oh. It's okay.
Capsules... You're giving them to me? Free?//...I'll remember. Always.
Food? ...So warm. Thank you.|Can I... eat this? ...It's good.
...I'll take it.|This... I'll keep it clean.
I don't want this.
Rest in the coffin. Let me stabilize you.
...So peaceful. It's been a long time.//Your treatment fee: {0}. Don't refuse.
...No power, or no medicine in the coffin. Another time.
Could you guard the shop for a few days? (Requires {0} boxes of capsules)
Leave it to me.//For {0} days, inspectors and sentencing officers won't get through that door.//Your cases are still there, though. Use the time to clean up.
Bai E's condition has improved: {0}.
Recovery
Enhanced
Fully Restored

(The lights dim merely from her presence.)//...You are the proprietor.//I am Ying Xiyuan. I desire one thing.//A Bellor movement and dial, housed in a Rydor case with a Rydor strap.//A classical heart. Bones of the future. Finish it, then light the incense.
...Where is it?|Speak.
We meet again.|...I am listening.|...Your shop has its curiosities. You, passable.
...You have come. No. I have.|Today, I am somewhat inclined to indulge.|Shen Yuan says your eye is sharp. ...She rarely praises anyone.
Bring me sought-after originals, or fine genuine watches with a questionable past. Stolen goods fetch three quarters. No one will pursue a sale I accept.
Condition, identity, timing. All are essential. Do not bring my own goods back to me.
...Granted.
(The incense clears. She is gone.)
Set it down.
...(She lifts the watch and studies it for a long time.)//Clean work. You may view my collection.
Not this.|Take it away.
...What cannot fit must wait.
Would you... erase those records?
...Merely brushing away dust.//The eyes upon you have closed.
A Star Coral Throne here? I came especially to see it.//Present any art or luxury goods worthy of the name.
How is the throne? Here I am again.|Any new acquisitions?
I thought about that last piece for three days. Anything like it today?|The throne's luster is richer than last time. You care for it well.
I tell my circle this little shop is the real private gallery.|I'm not here to buy today, just to sit by the throne... though if something fine turns up, I won't be shy.
Please.
Not up to standard.
A discerning eye.
A worthwhile visit.
...You looked upon what you should not see.//A mirror has two sides. We saw you, too.//(She turns away. A chill passes through the shop.)
...You looked again.//Someone beyond the mirror is writing down your name.
...You again.//Your name is written down. Now they are memorizing your face.
...You keep looking.//They know where your shop is. Next time, it won't be me who comes.
Prismatic Crownblade
Ying Xiyuan's sword. Its iridescence shifts with the thoughts of whoever looks upon it.

[Guard] In the showcase or an open sword rack: +80 deterrence, inspectors leave at the sight of it, and contraband shown beside it draws black-market buyers and brokers.\n[Upkeep] Each Star Coral Crystal lasts 7 days. During upkeep investigations slow down, the shop gets 300kJ of power each night, and the sword can stop a sentence.\n[Stopping a sentence] The sentencing officer leaves and the investigation resets to zero (case value stays), at the cost of 7 days of upkeep. Without upkeep it stops nothing.
Sunless Palace Mirror
A mirror without reflections. It reflects secrets instead.
Place it directly in the shop and open it. Once a day, reveal a customer's true identity or every secret of an item on the scales. Each use leaves a trace. At three traces, something comes calling.
Everday Amber Coffin
An amber coffin. Time passes slowly inside.
Place it directly in the shop and fit a battery to preserve the food and medicine inside overnight (20 kJ per night). When Bai E is present, you can offer her treatment inside.
Star Coral Throne
Living coral grown into a throne, waiting for its sovereign.

Place directly in the shop and put Vita-Stabilizer Capsules in the offering slot (3 days per box). Every three nourished nights produce a Star Coral Crystal and attract wealthy connoisseurs. Its scent may also attract quarantine inspectors.

Bai E's medicine. A gift uses the whole stack: +1 growth per gift and 3 stable days per capsule. Also used for coffin treatment and throne offerings.

Sells for a handsome price and maintains the Prismatic Crownblade. Gold Viper loves these.

Place in the workbench parts storage and fit it to the watch in the watch slot. That watch can then accept movements, dials and straps from other models. Essential for royal combinations.

For whoever takes over this shop

Unusual visitors sometimes stand across this counter.

They do not advertise themselves, and rarely repeat an offer. This ledger records who they are, what they want, and the secrets of thirteen watchmakers.

To give a gift, ask about preferences, then place your gift on the scales. To appraise a watch, pick up a magnifier. The rest will come with time.

Visitor Profiles II

The Limits of a Con

Sell flawed goods to an amateur at a steep price and the buyer may come after you. Honest descriptions and modest profits are never fraud.

[What counts] The item hides fake parts, a quartz movement, parts from another model or inflated condition, and you charged more than 1.6× its real value. Goods an expert checked on the spot don't count.

[Getting caught] The greedier, the likelier: about 20% at 1.6×, 75% at 5×, certain at 10×. You are warned at the sale that the margin is steep.

[Consequences] Settled before the next opening: ordinary customers cost you faction reputation, collectors cost favor, and a Fraud charge is recorded.

[Perks] Smooth Talker loosens the limit to 2×; Honest Face tightens it to about 1.3×.
Streetwise Buyers & Taboos

[Street eyes] Gold Viper, Crimson Falcon, Bai E and the Connoisseur don't know watches, but they know scams. Quartz movements and resin parts are spotted at once; crude replicas and off-model parts often are; metal replicas are the hardest to catch. Heavy wear passed off as near-new doesn't fool them either.
Caught with a stamped item: you pay compensation on the spot, favor drops hard, and she stays away for two weeks. Found out after the sale: she comes back in person for 1.5× the overcharge.

[Ying Xiyuan] Put a stamped item that still hides a flaw on her scales and the run ends immediately. Unstamped stock and honestly described replicas are safe.

[How records work] When you sell stolen goods or contraband:
Risk = contraband level × 20 + stolen heat
Share recorded = risk − shop deterrence
Example: a T5 gun with no heat has risk 60; at deterrence 40 only 20% is recorded, and at 60 nothing is. Each sale is capped at 5,000 per contraband level.

[One original each] Each of the 11 sealed originals can be acquired once per run, whether bought, won at auction or taken in a raid. Sell it, gift it or lose it and no second one appears. Just looking doesn't count.

[Deterrence] Weapons on show make your shop one to leave alone. Only your own complete weapons at condition 60+ count, and higher tiers score more (T1–T5: 3 / 6 / 12 / 22 / 30).
Gun rack and melee rack: up to 35 each. Open stock: the best three, up to 30. The Crownblade counts 80 on its own. Total cap 100. Covered racks, bags and boxes don't count.

[What deterrence does]
· Records: when you sell stolen goods or contraband, risk (contraband level × 20 + stolen heat) is reduced by deterrence, and only the remainder is recorded. The item tooltip shows the sum.
· Theft: burglars back off with a chance equal to your deterrence, up to 90%.
· Inspections: every 35 deterrence cancels one step of inspection pressure from prestige.

[Prestige] Fine watches on show make your shop known. The collector cabinet gives up to 60; three different watches on open display give up to 40.

[What prestige does]
· Upside: up to a 50% daily chance of one extra wealthy collector with a bigger budget.
· Downside: more burglars (twice as many at 100 prestige) and earlier inspections (one step per 35 prestige, two at most).
